planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in moist, humus-rich soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Set divisions a few inches deep into moist, humus-rich soil in full sun to very light shade, firming well so the fans don't rock loose before new roots form. Hybridized by Briscoe, Steve Varner earned the Society for Siberian Irises' Morgan-Wood Medal in 1987, one of the earliest cultivars honored after the award's founding. Keep the planting evenly watered through its first season, and expect established clumps to go five or more years before they need lifting and dividing.

planting.note: Plant divisions shallowly in rich, consistently moist soil in full sun to light partial shade.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions shallowly in rich, consistently moist soil in full sun to light partial shade, where the grassy clumps of foliage stay attractive well past bloom. Hybridized by Calvin Helsley, Mabel Coday took the Morgan-Wood Medal in 1991; Helsley went on to win the same medal again in 2005 with 'Where Eagles Dare.' Divide only when the center of a clump thins out, typically after four or more years, working right after bloom or in late summer.

planting.note: Plant divisions in evenly moist, fertile soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Give Jewelled Crown evenly moist, fertile soil and full sun to light shade, and expect it to settle in for years without needing division once established. Robert Hollingworth bred this cultivar, which won the Society for Siberian Irises' Morgan-Wood Medal in 1993, part of a long run of award-winning introductions from his Michigan breeding program. Water deeply during dry spells in its first two seasons, and lift and split congested clumps in late summer or right after flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade.

directions: Aqua Whispers wants consistently moist, fertile ground and full sun to light partial shade, conditions that let its narrow clumps of foliage bulk up quickly. Bred by Anna Mae Miller, who also produced the later Morgan-Wood winner 'Frosted Cranberry' in 1998, this cultivar earned the medal itself in 1995. Keep newly set divisions watered through their first summer, and plan to divide mature stands only once they become crowded, usually after four to five years.

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich soil in full sun to light partial shade.

directions: Set divisions a couple of inches deep in moist, humus-rich soil in full sun to light partial shade, spacing clumps far enough apart to fill in without crowding for several seasons. Hybridized by Warner, Shaker's Prayer received the Society for Siberian Irises' Morgan-Wood Medal in 1996. Mulch lightly to hold moisture through summer, and divide only when flowering noticeably declines at the center of an older clump.

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, evenly moist soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Plant divisions in rich, evenly moist soil in full sun to light shade, and water generously through the first growing season while roots establish. Banish Misfortune was bred by the Massachusetts team of Marty Schafer and Jan Sacks, whose Joe Pye Weed's Garden program produced this 2011 Morgan-Wood Medal winner along with many other award-winning Siberian introductions. Clumps can go undivided for years; split them in late summer or right after bloom once vigor starts to fade.

planting.note: Plant divisions in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade.

directions: Tree of Songs grows best in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade, where its narrow foliage clumps form a dense, low-maintenance stand. Schafer and Sacks of Joe Pye Weed's Garden bred this cultivar, which earned the Morgan-Wood Medal in 2014. Water deeply during its first two seasons to encourage a strong root system, then divide congested clumps only occasionally, in late summer or just after bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in evenly moist, humus-rich soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Give Humors of Whiskey evenly moist, humus-rich soil and full sun to light shade, and keep new divisions watered closely through their establishment year. Bred by Marty Schafer and Jan Sacks, it won the Society for Siberian Irises' Morgan-Wood Medal in 2015, one of several top awards the pair's Joe Pye Weed's Garden program has collected over the decades. Expect clumps to thrive for years before needing division, best done in late summer or right after flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, consistently moist soil in full sun to light partial shade.

directions: Plant Ginger Twist in rich, consistently moist soil in full sun to light partial shade, and mulch around new divisions to buffer moisture swings while they root in. Hybridizers Marty Schafer and Jan Sacks introduced this cultivar, which earned the Morgan-Wood Medal in 2016. Established clumps resist rot and borer problems far better than bearded iris and need dividing only once flowering begins to taper off at the clump's center.

planting.note: Plant divisions in evenly moist, fertile soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Neptune's Gold prefers evenly moist, fertile soil in full sun to light shade, settling into a dense clump of grassy foliage that stays tidy through the season. Robert Hollingworth bred this cultivar, which tied for the Society for Siberian Irises' Morgan-Wood Medal in 2021 (with Schafer and Sacks' 'Cape Cod Boys'), decades after his first medal winner in the 1990s. Keep the planting well watered its first year, then divide only when older clumps become congested, in late summer or just after bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, acidic soil that stays constantly moist through the growing season.

directions: Plant Midnight Fireworks in full sun to light shade in rich, acidic soil that never dries out through the growing season, since Japanese iris roots suffer quickly in parched ground. Introduced by Terry Aitken in 2014, it moved through the Society for Japanese Irises' honors system before winning the Payne Medal, the society's highest award, in 2026. Mulch to hold moisture and avoid any lime-containing amendments, and divide crowded clumps in early fall once bloom has finished for the year.

planting.note: Plant divisions in consistently moist, acidic soil in full sun to part shade.

directions: Columbia Crest needs full sun to part shade and soil that stays consistently moist and on the acidic side, thriving at pond margins or in a rain garden bed. Chad Harris introduced this cultivar in 2015, and it went on to win the Society for Japanese Irises' Payne Medal in 2024 after earlier Honorable Mention and Award of Merit honors. Never let the planting dry out during summer, and lift and divide congested clumps in early fall.

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, acidic soil kept constantly moist in full sun to light shade.

directions: Grow Koto Harp Strings in full sun to light shade in rich, acidic soil kept constantly moist, the standard requirement for Japanese iris to bloom and bulk up well. Bred by Chad Harris and introduced in 2016, it earned the Society for Japanese Irises' Payne Medal in 2023. Water deeply rather than shallowly through the growing season, and divide clumps every few years in early fall to keep flowering strong.

planting.note: Plant divisions in acidic soil kept wet through spring and summer in full sun to part shade.

directions: Flamingo Waltz performs best in full sun to part shade and acidic soil that is kept wet through spring and summer, conditions easiest to maintain at a pond edge or in a boggy border. Introduced by Chad Harris in 2014, it collected the Payne Medal, the Society for Japanese Irises' top award, in 2022. Avoid lime and let the soil dry only slightly after bloom, then divide overcrowded clumps in early fall.

planting.note: Plant divisions in consistently wet, acidic soil in full sun to part shade.

directions: Set Columbia Deep Water in full sun to part shade in consistently wet, acidic soil, since this cultivar tolerates standing water better than most garden perennials. Chad Harris introduced it in 2013, and it shared the Society for Japanese Irises' Payne Medal in 2021 with his own 'Dalle Whitewater.' Keep the root zone saturated through the growing season and divide crowded clumps in early fall once bloom ends.

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, acidic soil that never dries out in full sun to part shade.

directions: Dalle Whitewater wants full sun to part shade and rich, acidic soil that never dries out, making it well suited to a pond margin or rain garden planting. Introduced by Chad Harris in 2011, it shared the Society for Japanese Irises' 2021 Payne Medal with his cultivar 'Columbia Deep Water.' Water generously through summer and divide congested clumps in early fall to maintain vigorous bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in consistently moist, acidic soil in full sun to part shade.

directions: Cascade Rain grows best in full sun to part shade in consistently moist, acidic soil, the same boggy conditions Japanese iris need generally to thrive. Bred by Chad Harris in 2008, it was a co-winner of the Society for Japanese Irises' Payne Medal in 2019, tying with Bauer and Coble's 'Indigo Angel' in the society's annual voting. Keep the soil from ever drying out during the growing season, and divide clumps in early fall once they become crowded.

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, acidic, continuously moist soil in full sun to part shade.

directions: Plant Indigo Angel in full sun to part shade in rich, acidic, continuously moist soil, treating it the same as any pond-edge or rain-garden perennial. Bred by Bauer and Coble in 2011, it tied with 'Cascade Rain' for the Society for Japanese Irises' Payne Medal in 2019. Avoid letting the bed dry out at any point in the growing season, and lift and divide congested clumps in early fall after bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in acidic soil kept constantly wet in full sun to part shade.

directions: Kimono Silk needs full sun to part shade and acidic soil kept constantly wet through spring and summer to bloom well. Bred by Bauer and Coble in 2008, it won the Society for Japanese Irises' Payne Medal in 2018, the society's highest cultivar honor. Never allow the soil to dry during the growing season, and divide clumps in early fall only once flowering begins to decline.

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, acidic soil that stays wet through the growing season in full sun to part shade.

directions: Grow Pink Playmate in full sun to part shade in rich, acidic soil that stays wet throughout the growing season, the standard regimen for keeping Japanese iris healthy. Bred by Chad Harris, it earned Honorable Mention in 2021 and an Award of Merit in 2023 before taking the Society for Japanese Irises' Payne Medal in 2025. Keep the bed consistently saturated and divide overcrowded clumps in early fall after bloom finishes.
